title: A bound for a signed Fourier sum
statement: Let $n,t$ be natural numbers, let $0\le\delta\le1$ with $\delta\le1/2$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose values lie in $[-1,1]$. For each coordinate subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, write $\widehat f(S)$ for its uniform Fourier coefficient, and let $A_\delta(S)$ and $B_\delta(S)$ be the averages over random subsets $K$, in which each coordinate is included independently with probability $1-\delta$, of $(-1)^{|S\cap K|}\widehat f(S\cap K)$ and $|\widehat f(S\cap K)|$, respectively. Then $-\sum_S \widehat f(S)^2 A_\delta(S)\le \sqrt{(1-\delta)^t}+\sum_{S:\,|S|\le t}\widehat f(S)^2 B_\delta(S)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ takes values in $[-1,1]$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
